_about: A TPS application (src/tps.py), per uscis.gov/humanitarian/temporary-protected-status (updated 09/09/2026), uscis.gov/i-821 (updated 09/30/2026), the I-821 Instructions checklist and each country's own page, read 10/02/2026: the G-28, the I-821 and, when the client asks for a work permit, the I-765 under (a)(12) or (c)(19) in the same package. Evidence: identity and nationality (a passport, or a birth certificate with photo ID, or a national ID), the date of entry, continuous residence in the U.S. since the country's date, and certified court dispositions for any arrest or conviction. Only while a registration period is open (schemas/tps.json). The attorney approves titles and order.
title: TPS application (I-821 with the I-765)
requires_message: The client hasn't been processed yet: process the client first.

handwork.text: Two identical color passport-style photos, taken recently, for the I-765, with the client's name and A-Number lightly in pencil on the back (Form I-765 Instructions), when a work permit is asked for.
The package is received inside the registration period (the panel names it): USCIS rejects an application outside it unless late filing is allowed (8 CFR 244.17; the TPS page).
Each fee on its own card payment (the I-821, its biometric fee, the I-765, its Pub. L. 119-21 fee): a combined payment can get the package rejected.
Every Yes in Part 7 is explained in Part 11 with the place and date (the I-821 form), with the certified court dispositions for any arrest or conviction.

exhibits.title: Identity and nationality: the passport, or the birth certificate with photo ID, or a national ID
The date of entry into the U.S.: the I-94, or the passport page with the entry stamp
Continuous residence in the U.S.: employment records, rent receipts or utility bills, school or medical records
Certified court dispositions, arrest reports and charging documents, for any arrest, charge or conviction
TPS already granted: the approval notice and the work permit
